title: The Fundamental Solution Lies Beyond 1, So R₀ > 0
content: Mathlib's IsFundamental predicate bundles 1 < a₁.x and 0 < a₁.y. pellNorm_fundamental_gt_one reads these through the real embedding: since √d ≥ 0 and a₁.x ≥ 2, the norm ‖a₁‖ = x + y√d is ≥ 2 > 1 (the omega/linarith step uses y·√d ≥ 0). pellRegulator_fundamental_pos then feeds ‖a₁‖ > 1 into the parent's pellRegulator_pos to conclude R₀ = R(a₁) = log‖a₁‖ > 0.
mathContext: $\lVert a_1\rVert = x + y\sqrt d \ge 2 > 1 \Rightarrow R_0 = \log\lVert a_1\rVert > 0$.

title: The Regulator Ignores the Sign ±1
content: pellRegulator_neg proves R(-b) = R(b). The negation of a Pell solution negates both coordinates (Solution₁.x_neg, y_neg), so the norm of -b is the negative of the norm of b; Real.log_neg_eq_log (log(-t) = log t) then leaves the regulator unchanged. This is exactly what lets the ±a₁ⁿ structure theorem collapse to a single integer multiple of R₀, so the regulator spectrum is one lattice rather than a union of cosets.

title: Quantization R(b) = n·R₀ and Minimality of R₀
content: exists_regulator_eq_zsmul is the structural core: IsFundamental.eq_zpow_or_neg_zpow writes any solution b as a₁ⁿ or -a₁ⁿ; in either case the parent's pellRegulator_zpow gives R(a₁ⁿ) = n·R₀ and sign-invariance kills the ±, so R(b) = n·R₀ for some n : ℤ. The regulator spectrum is therefore the discrete lattice R₀·ℤ. pellRegulator_fundamental_le then makes R₀ the least positive value: if R(b) > 0 and R(b) = n·R₀ with R₀ > 0, then n ≥ 1 (nlinarith), so R(b) ≥ R₀.

title: Index of ⟨ofAdd k⟩ in Multiplicative ℤ is |k|
content: index_zpowers_ofAdd computes the index of the cyclic subgroup generated by Multiplicative.ofAdd k. The subgroup Subgroup.zpowers (ofAdd k) is shown equal to (AddSubgroup.zmultiples k).toSubgroup by an explicit element-wise argument (mem_zpowers_iff ↔ mem_zmultiples_iff via ofAdd_zsmul). Then AddSubgroup.index_toSubgroup and Int.index_zmultiples give the value k.natAbs. This is the model computation that the Pell index is transported onto.

title: The Index Equals k and Equals the Regulator Ratio
content: relindex_zpowers_pow proves [⟨a₁⟩ : ⟨a₁ᵏ⟩] = k. The power homomorphism zpowersHom : Multiplicative ℤ →* Solution₁ d, n ↦ a₁ⁿ, is injective because a₁ is torsion-free (parent not_isOfFinOrder from ‖a₁‖ > 1, via injective_zpow_iff_not_isOfFinOrder). It carries ⊤ to ⟨a₁⟩ (range_zpowersHom) and ⟨ofAdd k⟩ to ⟨a₁ᵏ⟩ (MonoidHom.map_zpowers), so Subgroup.relIndex_map_map_of_injective reduces the index to index_zpowers_ofAdd = k. Finally relindex_eq_regulator_ratio chains this with R(a₁ᵏ) = k·R₀ and field_simp to read the integer index off the real-analytic ratio R(a₁ᵏ)/R₀.
